name.text: Shared: Identify the intersection of two linear graphs

questiontext.text:
Two linear relations, Relation A and Relation B, are shown on the Cartesian plane.

The solution of the two relations is the point where the graphs intersect.

[[jsxgraph]] JXG.Options.text.useMathJax = true; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard( divid, { axis: true, showCopyright: false, boundingbox: [-6,6,6,-6], keepaspectratio: true, grid: true } ); var lineA = board.create( 'functiongraph', [ function(x) { return {#m1#}*x + {#c1#}; } ], { fixed: true, strokeWidth: 3 } ); var lineB = board.create( 'functiongraph', [ function(x) { return {#m2#}*x + {#c2#}; } ], { fixed: true, strokeWidth: 3, dash: 2 } ); board.unsuspendUpdate(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Enter the ordered pair representing the intersection point. Write your answer in the form \[ [x,y]. \] [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The intersection is the point that lies on both Relation A and Relation B.

Reading the graph gives \[ ({@xI@},{@yI@}). \]

Therefore the ordered pair is \[ [{@xI@},{@yI@}]. \]

Remember that the horizontal coordinate \(x\) is written first, followed by the vertical coordinate \(y\).

intersection-identification

Learners inspect two fixed linear graphs and identify the ordered pair representing their intersection.

Unlike QLIN-07, the learner is not reading a coordinate from a marked point. The learner must identify the single point shared by both linear relations.

Adapted from the straight-line graph question family represented by Numbas question NUMBAS-17290, "Graphs I: Linear - Line equation", licensed CC BY 4.0. The STACK implementation uses new wording, generated relations, intersection construction and diagnostic grading.

truefeedback.text: Correct. That ordered pair is the point shared by both linear graphs.
You appear to have entered the \(y\)-intercept of Relation A. The required point is where both graphs meet.
You appear to have entered the \(y\)-intercept of Relation B. Look for the point where Relation A and Relation B cross each other.
The coordinates appear to be reversed. Ordered pairs are written as \((x,y)\): horizontal coordinate first, vertical coordinate second.

falsefeedback.text: Find the point that lies on both graphs and enter its coordinates in the order \([x,y]\).

qtest.description: The generated intersection should receive full credit.
